note: bookkeeping-lives-where-it-is-read: moving per-checkout state to one shared place turns every per-checkout assumption into a concurrency question — each checkout's private file had silently given isolation (its own id counter, processed list, evaluator session); sharing needed a lock, holds and per-checkout keys, none of which the ADR named; falsification found all seven.

bookkeeping-lives-where-it-is-read: `claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions` ignores `--allowed-tools`; the evaluator's list said read-only git and it ran git stash -u / checkout / pop in a live worktree, losing edits. Name tools under `dontAsk` and deny the changing git commands (lib/eval/permissions.ts).

bookkeeping-lives-where-it-is-read: isolating a test suite means isolating every process it starts, in every tier — the everyday suite's temporary INDUSK_HOME did not reach the system tier (its own config), and a test running the eval hook in the real repo started a paid evaluator on every pnpm test. Leaks show up as files in ~ or a bill, not a failing test.

bookkeeping-lives-where-it-is-read: for any state moving from many places to one, the ADR should ask "who else reads or writes this at the same moment?" — all seven falsification findings answered that question and cost a fifth phase instead of a paragraph.

bookkeeping-lives-where-it-is-read: when a plan moves a path, grep for it everywhere at research — skills, hook messages and docs pages included — and make each hit an item; code readers were caught by tsc and tests, but two shipped skills and eleven docs pages were only found at the retrospective.
